title: Three Subgroups Lemma OQ-01-OQ-01: The Bilinear Lower-Central-Series Bound ⁅γᵢ,γⱼ⁆ ≤ γ₍ᵢ₊ⱼ₎
description: The lower central series γₙ of a group G satisfies the bilinear (grading) bound ⁅γᵢ, γⱼ⁆ ≤ γ₍ᵢ₊ⱼ₎ — the inductive payoff the parent entry's relative three subgroups lemma was built for, and explicitly named as the follow-up there. In Mathlib's 0-indexed convention (lowerCentralSeries G 0 = ⊤ = G, lowerCentralSeries G (n+1) = ⁅lowerCentralSeries G n, ⊤⁆, so Mathlib's index n is the standard γ₍ₙ₊₁₎), this is the clean form ⁅lowerCentralSeries G a, lowerCentralSeries G b⁆ ≤ lowerCentralSeries G (a+b+1). Mathlib develops the lower central series (lowerCentralSeries_succ, lowerCentralSeries_antitone, the Normal instance, products/pis, the derivedSeries comparison) but records NO bilinear commutator bound. This entry supplies it by induction on b, generalized over a so the inductive hypothesis is available at the shifted index a+1. The base case b=0 is the defining recursion ⁅γₐ, ⊤⁆ = γ₍ₐ₊₁₎; the inductive step writes γ₍ᵦ₊₁₎ = ⁅γᵦ, ⊤⁆ and applies the parent's normal-subgroup three subgroups lemma (ThreeSubgroupsLemmaOQ01.commutator_le_of_rotate) with N = γ₍ₐ₊ᵦ₊₂₎ (normal by Mathlib's lowerCentralSeries_normal instance): its two hypotheses are exactly the induction hypothesis at indices a+1 and a, the latter pushed one level by commutator_mono. The entry packages the symmetric companion (factors swapped), the b=0 corner ⁅γₐ, G⁆ ≤ γ₍ₐ₊₁₎, and a weakened-target form via antitonicity.

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide. All four named theorems depend only on the foundational propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound (verified with #print axioms). Mathlib's Mathlib/GroupTheory/Nilpotent.lean defines the lower central series and proves lowerCentralSeries_succ, lowerCentralSeries_antitone, the Normal instance, the product/pi behaviour, and derived_le_lower_central, but contains NO bilinear commutator bound ⁅γᵢ,γⱼ⁆ ≤ γ₍ᵢ₊ⱼ₎. The bilinear bound (the grading property of the lower central series), its symmetric companion, the b=0 corner, and the antitone weakening are the original content, derived by induction on the second index using the parent entry's relative three subgroups lemma (ThreeSubgroupsLemmaOQ01.commutator_le_of_rotate) together with Mathlib's lowerCentralSeries_normal, commutator_mono, and commutator_comm.

overview.historicalContext: The most important application of the three subgroups lemma is inductive: it powers the proof that the lower central series satisfies ⁅γᵢ(G), γⱼ(G)⁆ ≤ γ₍ᵢ₊ⱼ₎(G). This bilinearity is exactly what makes the associated graded object ⨁ₖ γₖ/γₖ₊₁ a graded Lie ring (with the commutator inducing the Lie bracket), the structure at the heart of the Magnus/Lazard correspondence and of much of the structure theory of nilpotent groups. The parent entry formalized the relative ('modulo a normal N') form of the three subgroups lemma precisely because this is the version the induction needs, and named this bound as its natural follow-up; the present entry carries out that induction.
overview.problemStatement:
Let G be a group with lower central series γₙ (Mathlib's lowerCentralSeries, 0-indexed: γ₀ = ⊤ = G and γ₍ₙ₊₁₎ = ⁅γₙ, ⊤⁆). Prove the bilinear bound
$$\lbrack \gamma_a, \gamma_b \rbrack \le \gamma_{a+b+1},$$
the 0-indexed form of the textbook 1-indexed grading inequality ⁅γᵢ, γⱼ⁆ ≤ γ₍ᵢ₊ⱼ₎ (with γ₁ = G).
overview.text: Mathlib defines lowerCentralSeries and proves its basic order/closure theory but not the bilinear commutator bound. This entry fills the gap with a short induction on the second index b, using the parent entry's relative three subgroups lemma as the engine. The base case is the defining recursion; the inductive step is a single application of the three subgroups lemma at a target normal subgroup deeper in the series, whose two hypotheses are precisely the induction hypothesis evaluated at two indices.
overview.proofStrategy: Induction on b, generalizing a (so the inductive hypothesis is the universally quantified ∀ a, ⁅γₐ, γᵦ⁆ ≤ γ₍ₐ₊ᵦ₊₁₎, usable at the shifted index a+1). Base case b=0: γ₀ = ⊤ and a+0+1 = a+1, so the goal ⁅γₐ, ⊤⁆ ≤ γ₍ₐ₊₁₎ is the definitional equality lowerCentralSeries G (a+1) = ⁅γₐ, ⊤⁆ (le_of_eq rfl). Inductive step: present γ₍ᵦ₊₁₎ as ⁅γᵦ, ⊤⁆ (definitional) and flip the goal ⁅γₐ, ⁅γᵦ,⊤⁆⁆ to ⁅⁅γᵦ,⊤⁆, γₐ⁆ via commutator_comm. Apply ThreeSubgroupsLemmaOQ01.commutator_le_of_rotate with H=⊤, K=γₐ, L=γᵦ and target N = γ₍ₐ₊(ᵦ₊₁)₊₁₎ (normal by lowerCentralSeries_normal). The two required hypotheses are: (i) ⁅⁅⊤, γₐ⁆, γᵦ⁆ = ⁅γ₍ₐ₊₁₎, γᵦ⁆ ≤ N, which is the induction hypothesis at index a+1 after the index rewrite a+1+b+1 = a+(b+1)+1; and (ii) ⁅⁅γₐ, γᵦ⁆, ⊤⁆ ≤ ⁅γ₍ₐ₊ᵦ₊₁₎, ⊤⁆ = γ₍ₐ₊ᵦ₊₂₎ = N, obtained from the induction hypothesis at index a by commutator_mono followed by the definitional unfolding of the next series term.
keyInsights: **The induction must generalize the first index**: the inductive step bounds ⁅γₐ, γ₍ᵦ₊₁₎⁆ and needs the hypothesis at γ₍ₐ₊₁₎ (the commutator of γₐ with the whole group lands in γ₍ₐ₊₁₎). Generalizing a before inducting on b makes the hypothesis available at a+1 exactly when required.

**The relative (≤ N) three subgroups lemma is the right tool, not the N = ⊥ case**: the target is a nontrivial subgroup γ₍ₐ₊ᵦ₊₂₎ deep in the series, so the parent's ≤ N generalization is essential — Mathlib's bottom-case Hall–Witt lemma (= ⊥) would not apply here. This is the concrete inductive payoff the parent entry was constructed for.

**The two hypotheses are the same induction hypothesis at two indices**: one feeds ⁅γ₍ₐ₊₁₎, γᵦ⁆ directly; the other pushes ⁅γₐ, γᵦ⁆ one level deeper with commutator_mono using ⁅γₖ, ⊤⁆ = γ₍ₖ₊₁₎. No new commutator combinatorics beyond the three subgroups lemma are needed.

**Definitional unfolding handles the index bookkeeping**: γ₍ₙ₊₁₎ = ⁅γₙ, ⊤⁆ holds by rfl, and a+(b+1)+1 is definitionally a+b+2; the only non-definitional index identity is a+1+b+1 = a+(b+1)+1 (a single omega/succ_add rewrite), because Nat addition recurses on the right argument.
prerequisites: Mathlib's lower central series lowerCentralSeries (the 0-indexed definition γ₀ = ⊤, γ₍ₙ₊₁₎ = ⁅γₙ, ⊤⁆) with lowerCentralSeries_zero and the definitional succ unfolding
The Normal instance lowerCentralSeries_normal (each term is normal in G), required to invoke the relative three subgroups lemma
lowerCentralSeries_antitone (the series is decreasing), used for the weakened-target corollary
The parent entry's relative three subgroups lemma ThreeSubgroupsLemmaOQ01.commutator_le_of_rotate, plus Subgroup.commutator_mono and Subgroup.commutator_comm

sections.title: The Bilinear Lower-Central-Series Bound
sections.summary: lowerCentralSeries_commutator_le is the main result, proved by induction on b generalized over a. The base case is the defining recursion ⁅γₐ, ⊤⁆ = γ₍ₐ₊₁₎; the inductive step applies the parent's relative three subgroups lemma (commutator_le_of_rotate) with target N = γ₍ₐ₊ᵦ₊₂₎, whose two hypotheses are the induction hypothesis at indices a+1 and a (the latter pushed one step by commutator_mono).

sections.title: Symmetric, Corner, and Weakened Forms
sections.mathContext: Swapped factors $\lbrack \gamma_b, \gamma_a \rbrack \le \gamma_{a+b+1}$; the $b=0$ corner $\lbrack \gamma_a, G \rbrack \le \gamma_{a+1}$; and $c \le a+b+1 \Rightarrow \lbrack \gamma_a, \gamma_b \rbrack \le \gamma_c$.
sections.summary: lowerCentralSeries_commutator_le' is the symmetric companion (commutator_comm). lowerCentralSeries_commutator_top_le records the b=0 corner ⁅γₐ, ⊤⁆ ≤ γ₍ₐ₊₁₎ as the familiar defining recursion. lowerCentralSeries_commutator_le_of_le weakens the target to any smaller index c ≤ a+b+1 using lowerCentralSeries_antitone (the series is decreasing, so γ₍ₐ₊ᵦ₊₁₎ ≤ γ_c).

conclusion: The bilinear (grading) bound ⁅γᵢ, γⱼ⁆ ≤ γ₍ᵢ₊ⱼ₎ of the lower central series is formalized sorry-free and axiom-free, in Mathlib's 0-indexed form ⁅lowerCentralSeries G a, lowerCentralSeries G b⁆ ≤ lowerCentralSeries G (a+b+1). Mathlib develops the lower central series but does not record this commutator bound; the proof is a clean induction on the second index whose inductive step is a single application of the parent entry's relative three subgroups lemma at a target normal subgroup deep in the series. This is the concrete inductive payoff the parent's ≤ N generalization was built for, and the structural fact that makes the associated graded ⨁ₖ γₖ/γₖ₊₁ a graded Lie ring. Natural further follow-ups include the dual bound for the derived series, the generation of γₙ by weight-n left-normed commutators, and the graded-Lie-ring structure itself.
